verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's own Post-Incident Reviews draw on the incident lifecycle, Slack data and the Scribe Agent to build chronological incident narratives and coordinate preventative follow-up actions. A GA changelog for AI-generated PIRs says teams can start them from the incident page or Slack after resolution, for the team to review. The AI-generated aspect is evidenced mainly by the changelog's URL and by Scribe 'enhancing post-incident reviews', not by detailed drafting docs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the AI drafts contributing factors (only 'systemic patterns' is mentioned), detail on the AI draft's contents and the human review/edit step, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, AI drafts the postmortem from the incident record — timeline, contributing factors, follow-ups — ready for human review

citations.quote: Post-Incident Reviews integrate with your incident lifecycle, Slack data, and the PagerDuty Advance Scribe Agent to help your team uncover systemic patterns, build chronological incident narratives, and coordinate preventative follow-up actions
Teams can start PIRs directly from the incident detail page or Slack after resolving an incident
Transcribe incident meetings in real time to enhance incident summaries and post-incident reviews
generative AI for summarizing key information about an incident
